latest_release.name: @ui-sdk/web@0.1.0-beta.19
latest_release.body:
### Patch Changes

- 287cab6: A closed Popover, Hover Card, Dialog, Alert Dialog and Drawer waits for its first use to set itself up, like Menu and Tooltip, unless it has `open`, `defaultOpen`, a `controller` or a `presentation`. Parts that aren't shown take less work to mount in every framework.
- e3d2015: A disabled `<ui-toggle>`, `<ui-checkbox>` or `<ui-switch>` takes a `pressed` or `checked` written from script, by property or attribute, like a native input's `value`. Presses, the `api` and agents still can't change it while it's disabled. Inside a toggle group or a disabled checkbox group, the group still decides.
- 3c9f2ae: An image cropper starts its first image's crop at `defaultCrop` even when the default arrives after the cropper is made, like the web property set on a `<ui-image-cropper>` already in the page. `defaultCrop` is now on the element's type.
- fe4d8ad: The types of `<ui-command>`'s `valuechange` now include `detail.index`, and the types of `querychange` on `<ui-select>`, `<ui-combobox>` and `<ui-command>` include `detail.composing`. Vue's Command, Combobox and Select type `queryChange`'s details with `composing` too.
- 25d0606: The package's docs now include `docs/components.md`: every component's composition, attributes and events in one file, for an agent building a page with no build step.
- 3cc1b67: A drag preview's copy of web components stays as it was made: the elements cloned into it no longer connect and start their own instance, so a checked box in the copy stays checked and its parts keep their ids and slots.
- 3028fe8: In parts made with `createParts`, a part's own attribute or property now wins over a prop it takes from the part around it, like a cell's `value` inside a row. Setting a boolean one to `false` keeps it off even when the part around it is on.
- 3073909: A `<ui-file-input-dropzone>`'s `pasteTarget` property keeps an element or a function as it is, so pastes into that target add their files. The `paste-target` attribute still takes `"document"` or a CSS selector.
- cd8bf5a: A popup content's `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` properties keep an element or a function that returns one, as their types say. Before, the property wrote it to the attribute as a string, so opening or closing the popup threw and focus was lost. The `initial-focus` and `final-focus` attributes still take a selector.
- Updated @ui-sdk/core to 0.1.0-beta.19

hot_issues.title: Web components in Effect UI apps
Agent bridge: a number-valued Select refuses item labels, and a value silently wins over another item's label
Scroll Area: stickToEnd lets go after a sub-pixel move up at the end, and nothing re-arms it
Potential issues found while auditing Dialog and Popup internals
Select, Combobox: the hidden form input lengthens the scroll container around an unpositioned scroll area
NumberInput: step buttons' aria-controls ignore an explicit id on NumberInputControl
Sheet (scroll-snap driver): scrollIntoView({ block: "end" }) on an item dismisses the open sheet
Dialog: a press on the page while a modal dialog is leaving is swallowed

detail.readme: # UI SDK A library of behaviors for agents to build and drive the next generation of user interfaces. Keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and the ARIA they need live in `@ui-sdk/core`, with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components. **[Read the docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)** ## Install UI SDK is in beta. Install core and the adapter for your framework: ```bash npm install @ui-sdk/react @ui-sdk/core ``` For other frameworks, swap `@ui-sdk/react` for `@ui-sdk/vue`, `@ui-sdk/svelte`, `@ui-sdk/solid` or `@ui-sdk/web`. Then give your agent the UI SDK skill: ```bash npx skills@latest add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk ``` ## Example Every component in UI SDK is built from behaviors. You start by creating the primitive with behaviors. Don't worry, you don't need to learn how to write this. Your agents will. And we made them really good at it. ```ts import { createFocusRecovery, definePrimitive } from "@ui-sdk/core" const searchField = definePrimitive({ name: "search-field", state: () => ({ value: "" }), api: (context) => ({ set: (value: string) => context.store.set({ value }), recovery: createFocusRecovery({ fallback: () => context.element("input") }), }), slots: (slot) => ({ input: slot({ attrs: (state) => ({ value: state.value }), on: { input: (event, { api }) => api.set((event.target as HTMLInputElement).value), }, }), clear: slot({ present: (state) => state.value !== "", attrs: () => ({ type: "button" }), press: ({ api }) => api.set(""), bind: (el, part) => part.api.recovery.bind(el, part), }), }), }) export { searchField } ``` Then render it in your framework with `createParts`. The parts are the same in all five. ### React ```tsx import { createParts } from "@ui-sdk/react/primitive" import { searchField } from "./search-field" const parts = createParts(searchField, { input: "input", clear: "button" }) const SearchField = parts.Root const SearchFieldInput = parts.Input const SearchFieldClear = parts.Clear function Search() { return ( Clear ) } export { Search } ``` ### Vue ```vue ``` ### Svelte ```svelte Clear ``` ### Solid ```tsx import { createParts } from "@ui-sdk/solid/primitive" import { searchField } from "./search-field" const parts = createParts(searchField, { input: "input", clear: "button" }) const SearchField = parts.Root const SearchFieldInput = parts.Input const SearchFieldClear = parts.Clear function Search() { return ( Clear ) } export { Search } ``` ### Web Components Register a custom element for each part: ```ts import { createParts, wrappedButton, wrappedChild } from "@ui-sdk/web" import { searchField } from "./search-field" createParts(searchField, { root: "search-field", input: { tag: "search-field-input", target: wrappedChild("input") }, clear: { tag: "search-field-clear", target: wrappedButton }, }) ``` Then use them in your HTML: ```html ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get the repo running locally and land a change, and use [issues](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui/issues) to report bugs. By participating, you agree to our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Security Please do not open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Instead, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and report responsibly to [responsible.disclosure@vercel.com](mailto:responsible.disclosure@vercel.com). ## Beta terms UI SDK is currently in beta and subject to the [Vercel beta terms](https://vercel.com/docs/release-phases/public-beta-agreement); the framework, APIs, documentation, and behavior may change before general availability.
